summary: M.S. Computer Engineering graduate from Rochester Institute of Technology (RIT), NY. Built performance-critical C++ and embedded C systems, including a 5.2× TensorRT inference speedup and a 30× parallel ray tracer speedup across 55 processes. Experienced in real-time systems, FreeRTOS concurrency, profiling, and performance tuning.

experience.title: Research Intern (Capstone)
bullets: Designed a custom wavelet bank (alpha-blended sym6+bior3.5) with optimized homography stitching and concurrency, raising PSNR to 86 from a 65 baseline.
Deployed ZoeDepth monocular depth estimation for crack-depth profiling with ±8% error on 3D surface reconstruction.

experience.title: Embedded Systems Intern
bullets: Implemented a custom tap-detection algorithm using z-axis differential thresholding on ADXL345 data; resolved sensor jitter through software calibration and resolution tuning.

experience.title: Python Developer Intern
bullets: Developed a Python GUI using PyQt and Matplotlib for real-time data acquisition and experimental visualization; used GitLab for version control.

projects.name: CUDA Kernel Optimization for VGG16 Inference
bullets: Coalesced kernel ran at 49.2 ms vs 73.3 ms uncoalesced and 77.5 ms CPU TorchScript (~35% speedup over naive GPU) with identical accuracy.
Replaced TorchScript conv layers in VGG16 with custom CUDA C++ kernels using memory coalescing, constant memory, and preallocated global buffers.

projects.name: Parallel Ray Tracer with MPI Task Scheduling
bullets: Achieved up to 30× speedup with static strip partitioning (55 processes); dynamic task queue outperformed all static methods under unpredictable workloads.
Benchmarked four parallel work distribution strategies (static strip/block/cyclic, dynamic task queue) rendering 5000×5000 pixel scenes with MPI.

projects.name: STM32 Bare-Metal Temperature Monitor
bullets: Built Cortex-M4 firmware in embedded C for real-time temperature monitoring at a deterministic 1 Hz update rate within 3.68 KB Flash / 1.58 KB RAM; verified in Proteus.
Implemented timer-triggered ADC scan conversions, interrupt-driven sample capture, and a low-level I2C driver, programming GPIO, TIM2, ADC1, and I2C1 directly in bare-metal C.

projects.name: Voice-Controlled Robotic Arm (COFFIN) — MS Capstone, RIT
bullets: Optimized YOLO inference with TensorRT for a 5.2× speedup (56.7→10.9 ms, 17.6→92 FPS vs eager PyTorch) in a voice-to-pick pipeline running at ~11.5 s end-to-end latency.
Troubleshot and resolved 11 integration failures (false-positive detections, servo brown-out, stale-frame capture) to reach 100% pick reliability (10/10 trials).
Wrote two-link IK in C++ on Arduino; built a multiprocessing multi-camera frame-capture pipeline; deployed the Jetson bridge as a systemd service.

projects.name: Object Tracking Turret
bullets: Used FreeRTOS with mutexes for shared-memory task coordination alongside interrupt-driven UART commands and multi-servo PWM control, tracking YOLOv8 detections from an NVIDIA Jetson.
